title: Between / min-max range → double inequality
subtitle: Linear inequalities in one or two variables · 14 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **14 of the official questions in Linear inequalities in one or two variables are this one** — 8 Easy, 4 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The stem gives a quantity that stays between a low and a high value, using words like 'at least … but no more than', 'minimum of … maximum of', 'varied between', or 'more than … but less than'.
- The answer choices are all double inequalities (a ≤ x ≤ b style), or they are numbers you check against a range.
- Sometimes the range is per unit and the question asks about several units or several days.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Turn each bound into its own symbol: 'at least' or 'minimum' is ≥, 'no more than' or 'maximum' is ≤, and 'more than' or 'less than' is strict.
- 2) If the range is per unit or per day, multiply both ends by the count and add any starting amount to both ends.
- 3) Pick the choice with the lower bound on the left and the right strictness at each end, or the number that falls inside the range.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: You can type the double inequality to see the band, but the work is mostly reading the words.
It is quick for scaling a range: type low*n + start and high*n + start and read off both ends.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You flip 'minimum' and 'maximum' and write the bounds the wrong way round.
Or you use ≤ where the words say strictly 'more than'.
On scaled ranges, you multiply only one end, or you forget to add the starting value to both ends.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
